scenes.title: Consumers & Consumer Groups
scenes.subtitle: Reading events in parallel and scaling out
scenes.narration: Consumers read events from Kafka, and consumer groups let a team of consumers share the work of a topic.

scenes.title: How Groups Work
bullets: A consumer group has a shared group id
Each partition is assigned to exactly one member
Adding consumers scales reading up to partition count
Different groups each get a full copy of the stream
scenes.narration: All consumers sharing a group id belong to the same consumer group. Within that group, each partition is assigned to exactly one member, so work is divided without duplication. Adding more consumers scales reading, but only up to the number of partitions. Meanwhile, separate consumer groups each receive their own full copy of the stream, enabling independent applications.

scenes.title: Balancing Partitions
scenes.narration: When a consumer joins a group, the group coordinator on a broker assigns it a share of the partitions. The consumer then polls those partitions in a loop and processes each batch of records. After processing, it commits its offset to mark progress. If a consumer leaves or joins, a rebalance reassigns partitions across the members.

scenes.title: A Consumer in Python
scenes.narration: This consumer joins the billing-service group and subscribes to the orders topic. The auto.offset.reset of earliest tells it to start from the beginning if it has no saved position. The poll loop fetches records, and after handling each one it commits the offset so the same record is not reprocessed. Every consumer sharing this group id will split the partitions among themselves.

scenes.text: Use one group per application. Scale within a group by adding consumers, but never beyond the number of partitions, or the extras sit idle.
scenes.narration: The key insight is to use one consumer group per application. You scale within a group by adding consumers, but never beyond the number of partitions, or the extra consumers will simply sit idle.
